question: The phenomenon due to which the relative motion between a conductor and a magnet produces a potential difference across the conductor is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**electromagnetic induction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electromagnetic induction** is the phenomenon due to which the relative motion between a conductor and a magnet produces a potential difference across the conductor.
 
• This principle was discovered by **Michael Faraday** in 1831.
 
• It forms the working basis of many electrical devices such as transformers, electric generators, and inductors.
 
• The induced potential difference or voltage is generated due to the changing magnetic field around the conductor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Faraday's** experiments showed that a change in the magnetic field within a closed loop of wire induces an electric current in the wire.
 
• The direction of the induced current is given by **Lenz's Law**, which states that the induced current will flow in such a direction that it will oppose the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
 
• The magnitude of the induced electromotive force (EMF) is given by **Faraday's Law of Induction**, which states that the EMF induced is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux.
 
• Applications of electromagnetic induction include electric power generation, induction cooking, wireless power transfer, and electromagnetic braking.
